model_edit.reason: The original assertion required out_data to equal the immediately previous inp_data, which is only valid for a single-entry FIFO. The cc_id_queue stores multiple outstanding requests per ID and returns the oldest pending payload for the requested ID, so the returned data may have been accepted several cycles earlier. The repaired assertion checks that the returned data matches one of the last 8 accepted input data values, consistent with the specification that response age is 1..8 and three requests may be pending. This removes the false alarms on legal multi-entry behavior while still detecting the artificial data fault, where the returned data is off by one from any legitimately stored value.

edits.value: out_req && out_gnt && out_valid && $past(inp_req && inp_gnt && inp_id == out_id)

model_edit.reason: The current assertion fires on any out_valid handshake and compares against the immediately previous inp_data, which is wrong for an ID queue: output may select IDs in any order and may be a non-pop peek. Confirmed legal traces show out_data matching an older input with the same ID (e.g. cycle 8 out_id=2/out_data=223 after cycle 5 inp_id=2/inp_data=223), while the primary fault corrupts the stored payload (e.g. 212->213). The antecedent is narrowed to require that the previous cycle accepted an input with the same ID as the current output, and the consequent keeps the payload equality. This preserves the confirmed violating transactions (where the previous accepted input has the same ID as the output) while removing the legal false alarms caused by ID reordering and peeks.
